assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chromatography
items.clue: A technique for separating the components of a mixture.

items.label: Cyanobacteria
items.clue: Photosynthetic prokaryotes that, like plants and algae, split water and release oxygen.

items.label: Rf value
items.clue: The distance moved by a pigment from the origin divided by the distance moved by the solvent front from the origin.

items.label: Photosynthesis
items.clue: The process in which light energy absorbed by pigments is transformed into chemical energy held in carbon compounds.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the energy transformation that takes place in photosynthesis?

options.text: Light energy absorbed by pigments is transformed into chemical energy in the carbon compounds made.
Energy is generated inside the chloroplast and then stored in glucose for the plant to use.
Light energy is converted into heat, which then speeds up the reactions that make glucose.
Chemical energy absorbed from the soil by the roots is transferred into the glucose molecules the leaf makes.

questions.stem: Which word equation correctly summarises photosynthesis?

options.text: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy
carbon dioxide + light energy → glucose + oxygen
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
soil minerals + water → glucose + oxygen

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is converted to glucose using hydrogen obtained by splitting water, and the oxygen left over from the water is released as a by-product.

questions.stem: Which list includes all of the groups of organisms that release oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis?

options.text: Plants, algae, cyanobacteria, fungi
Plants, algae and cyanobacteria
Plants and algae, no bacteria
Land plants and no other group

questions.explanation: Oxygen is a by-product of photosynthesis in plants, algae and cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, but they split water in the same way and release oxygen.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. On a paper chromatogram of leaf pigments, the origin line was 20 mm from the bottom edge of the paper, the centre of the carotene spot was 65 mm from the bottom edge and the solvent front was 70 mm from the bottom edge. What is the Rf value of carotene?
A chlorophyll molecule in a leaf absorbs a photon of red light. What happens within the molecule as a result?

options.text: An electron is raised to a higher energy level.
It vibrates faster, warming the surrounding stroma.
It splits a molecule of water that is bound to it.
It stores the light inside itself until it is needed.

questions.explanation: Absorbing a photon excites an electron within the pigment molecule, raising it to a higher energy level. This is the step in which light energy is transformed into chemical energy, carried by the excited electron.

questions.stem: A student places a lamp at different distances from a beaker of pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution kept at 25 °C, and counts the bubbles of gas released per minute at each distance. Which correctly identifies the variables?

options.text: Independent: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: bubbles per minute; dependent: distance of lamp
Controlled variable: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: temperature of 25 °C; dependent: bubbles per minute

questions.stem: Tomato plants were grown in two enclosed greenhouses, one at 400 ppm carbon dioxide and one at 800 ppm. Both were kept at 22 °C with the same lighting and watering, and after six weeks the dry mass of the plants was measured. Which is a controlled variable in this experiment?

options.text: The carbon dioxide concentration in the greenhouses
The dry mass of the plants measured at six weeks
The plants grown at 400 ppm carbon dioxide
The temperature of 22 °C in both greenhouses

questions.stem: A fox eats a rabbit that has fed on grass. Where did the chemical energy in the carbon compounds of the fox's body originally come from?

options.text: New energy created by the grass in photosynthesis and passed on to the rabbit and fox.
Light energy transformed into chemical energy by photosynthesis in the grass.
Chemical energy that the grass absorbed from the soil through its roots.
Energy in the oxygen the grass made as its main product, breathed in by the two animals.

questions.stem: Glucose produced by photosynthesis contains hydrogen atoms. From which substance were these hydrogen atoms obtained?

options.text: Carbon dioxide molecules joined together to make glucose.
Mineral ions the roots absorbed from the soil water.
Chlorophyll, which breaks down during the reaction.
Water molecules, which are split during photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is converted to glucose using hydrogen obtained by splitting water. The oxygen left over from the split water molecules is released.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a photosystem?

options.text: A single chlorophyll molecule that absorbs light by itself and carries out the whole of the light-dependent reactions on its own.
An array of chlorophyll and accessory pigments held in a membrane, with a special chlorophyll at the reaction centre that emits an excited electron.
A cluster of pigment molecules dissolved in the stroma, from which excited electrons pass across into the thylakoid space.
An array of pigment molecules in the thylakoid membrane, each of which emits its own excited electron to the chain of electron carriers.

questions.stem: Which statement about the photolysis of water in photosystem II is correct?

options.text: Its electrons replace those lost by the reaction centre, its protons join the gradient and oxygen is waste.
Light absorbed directly by water molecules in the thylakoid lumen breaks them apart into hydrogen gas and oxygen gas.
The hydrogen released from water is passed straight to NADP at photosystem II, reducing it before the electrons move on.
Oxygen is the useful product of photolysis, and the protons and electrons are waste that diffuses out of the chloroplast.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes how ATP is produced in the thylakoid?

options.text: The electron carriers make ATP directly as electrons pass along them, transferring the energy of each electron into a phosphate bond on ADP.
Protons are pumped out of the lumen into the stroma and flow back into the lumen through ATP synthase, releasing ATP inside it.
Electron carriers pump protons into the thylakoid lumen, and the protons flow back into the stroma through ATP synthase, which makes ATP.
Reduced NADP passes its electrons to the carriers, which pump protons for ATP synthesis, exactly as reduced NAD does in mitochondria.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the reduction of NADP in the light-dependent reactions?

options.text: NADP accepts hydrogen atoms that are released directly by the splitting of water at photosystem II, forming reduced NADP.
NADP accepts two electrons that have come from photosystem I and a hydrogen ion from the stroma, forming reduced NADP.
NADP accepts electrons that are returning to photosystem I in cyclic photophosphorylation, forming reduced NADP.
NADP accepts two electrons from photosystem I and a hydrogen ion from the thylakoid lumen, forming reduced NADP inside the thylakoid.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly locates the light-dependent reactions within a thylakoid?

options.text: Water is split in the stroma, and ATP and reduced NADP are made in the thylakoid lumen, where the enzymes of the Calvin cycle then use them.
Protons are pumped out into the stroma, and ATP synthase makes ATP inside the thylakoid lumen as the protons flow back in across the membrane.
The photosystems float freely in the thylakoid lumen, and ATP synthase is embedded in the outer membrane of the chloroplast.
Water is split on the lumen side of photosystem II, ATP synthase releases ATP into the stroma and NADP is reduced on the stroma side.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes carbon fixation by Rubisco?

options.text: Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP, forming two molecules of glycerate 3-phosphate.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP to form a six-carbon sugar, which is then released as glucose.
Rubisco uses the energy of ATP to attach carbon dioxide to RuBP, forming glycerate 3-phosphate.
Rubisco adds hydrogen from reduced NADP to carbon dioxide, converting it directly into triose phosphate.
